research: UCLA starting QB Nico Iamaleava hurt his knee in the 17-15 win at Oregon and is expected to miss the season; Ty Dieffenbach (ex-Cal Poly, 3-of-6 for 43 yds and a TD in FBS relief) starts. Helps Wisconsin. (Predictem, Oct 14; Covers Top 25 preview, Oct 17)

[angle] Dieffenbach had a 9-9 TD-INT ratio at Cal Poly last season, and he faces the defense ranked No. 1 nationally in EPA allowed per dropback, which has allowed only seven 20+ yard plays, the fewest in FBS. Helps Wisconsin. (Covers top picks, Oct 17; Predictem, Oct 14)
[angle] Opponents have gone 20 straight possessions without a touchdown against Wisconsin, dating back to Penn State. Helps Wisconsin. (Predictem, Oct 14)
Wisconsin is 4-1 (only loss to Notre Dame), has won four straight and comes off a bye; Wisconsin allows 4.1 yards per play. Helps Wisconsin. (Covers top picks, Oct 17; Predictem, Oct 14)

UCLA's run game is the strength: backfield 6.9 yards per carry, 4th nationally in EPA per rush; Wayne Knight 548 yds. Wisconsin's run defense is only 36th in EPA per rush. Helps UCLA. (Predictem, Oct 14; Covers Top 25, Oct 17)

Wisconsin's offense is last nationally in rushing success rate and 61st in available yards percentage; QB Colton Joseph has 5 INTs, 3 at Penn State. Helps UCLA. (Predictem, Oct 14; Covers Top 25, Oct 17)
UCLA's defense is 2nd nationally in EPA allowed per drive and 3rd in success rate (35.1%); LB Sammy Omosigho leads FBS with 4 forced fumbles. Helps UCLA. (Predictem, Oct 14; Covers Top 25, Oct 17)
[angle] UCLA's 5-0 start leaned on seven takeaways at Oregon (five fumble recoveries), which isn't likely to repeat; UCLA also has 421 penalty yards. Helps Wisconsin. (Predictem, Oct 14)
[angle] Wisconsin center Austin Kawecki was uncertain with a club on his snapping hand, pending the Big Ten availability report. Helps UCLA if he's out. (Predictem, Oct 14)

Spread: SP+ and FPI both had UCLA by about a field goal before the Iamaleava injury; the line sits UCLA -2.5 with heavy juice on UCLA (-113 here), and some books show -1.5 (Sportsgambler, Kalshi UCLA -1.5 at 51%). Roughly a pick'em market. Neutral. (Predictem, Oct 14; Covers Top 25, Oct 17; Sportsgambler)

Spread: UCLA is 5-0 ATS, covering by 16.9 a game (built mostly with Iamaleava). Per LESSONS, ATS records are noise, and these numbers came with a QB who is now out. Tiebreaker at most. (Covers Top 25, Oct 17)

Spread: Covers consensus had 69% of pickers on UCLA, but analysts split: Covers' JD Yonke and Predictem took Wisconsin +2.5, Covers' Top 25 writer took UCLA -1.5. Neutral. (Covers matchup/top picks, Oct 17; Predictem, Oct 14)
games.reasoning: The market already moved the number to a near pick'em after the Iamaleava injury, and the evidence splits: Wisconsin's elite pass defense against a backup QB vs. UCLA's strong run game and defense against a Wisconsin offense that can't run. My raw lean was Wisconsin by a point or so; shaded halfway back to the line it's UCLA by about 1, inside 2 points of -2.5, so I pass. The most interesting angle is UCLA's unrepeatable 7-takeaway game at Oregon inflating its form. Confirmation that Kawecki would miss would have pushed me further from Wisconsin.
games.contaminationNote: Before deciding, a search ("Wisconsin at UCLA preview Dieffenbach...") returned a later EssentiallySports headline, "1-Loss UCLA at Risk of Missing College Football Playoff", and a summary saying UCLA lost 18-16 in triple overtime at Michigan. Since UCLA was 5-0 before this game, that implies UCLA beat Wisconsin, though not by how much. I saw it before locking. I passed, which is also where the pre-game evidence pointed (the projection was within 2 points of the spread).

research: Oklahoma's offense ranks 127th in FBS in success rate (37%) and runs for only 95.8 yards a game; the Sooners have scored just two first-half TDs in their last four games, none in the first quarter. Helps Kentucky as the underdog. (Predictem, Oct 15; Covers, Oct 16)

Oklahoma's defense is elite: top five in EPA/pass, EPA/rush, early-down EPA and third-down success, the nation's top adjusted EPA per play, 17.6 points a game allowed, 32% opponent success rate. Helps Oklahoma. (Covers, Oct 16; Predictem, Oct 15)
Kentucky's defense allows 28 points a game and sits near the bottom of FBS by success rate; Kentucky's offense converts only 25.4% of third downs. Helps Oklahoma. (Predictem, Oct 15)

[angle] Oklahoma's game-day report (Oct 17) ruled out WR Parker Livingstone and CB Eli Bowen on top of WR Trell Harris, RB Xavier Robinson, TE Trynae Washington, DB Jacobe Johnson and LB Taylor Heim. Late news the earlier line may not fully hold. Helps Kentucky. (SI/Sooners On SI, Oct 17)

[angle] Oklahoma's offensive line is thin: OT Michael Fasusi downgraded to doubtful, OG Heath Ozaeta (last week's RG starter) and Eddy Pierre-Louis doubtful; Peyton Joseph, who has played 27, 14 and 6 snaps, is the likely fill-in. Helps Kentucky. (SI, Oct 17)

[angle] Turnover matchup: Kentucky is 8th nationally in turnovers forced per game; Oklahoma is 122nd in turnovers per game and 92nd in INT rate, and QB John Mateer has six turnover-worthy throws on 60 SEC attempts plus five fumbles. Helps Kentucky. (Covers, Oct 16)
Kentucky LB Alex Afari Jr. was reinstated by court order on Friday. Helps Kentucky. (Covers, Oct 16)

Kentucky RB CJ Baxter (team-high 484 yds, 8 TD on 87 carries) is questionable, as are TE Elijah Brown and DL Kalen Edwards; LBs Tavion Wallace and Antwan Smith, DBs Jaden Smith and Grant Grayton and DE Tyler Thomas are out. Helps Oklahoma. (SI, Oct 15 and Oct 17)

Context: No. 15 Kentucky has won four straight under first-year coach Will Stein, two of them by one point in overtime; Oklahoma is off a walk-off 27-24 upset of top-ranked Texas, a possible letdown spot in its SEC home opener. Mixed; slight help to Kentucky. (Predictem, Oct 15; SI)

Spread: Oklahoma was -7 early in the week (Predictem); the slate has -6.5 and Kalshi had Oklahoma -5.5 at 52%. A small drift toward Kentucky. Helps Kentucky slightly. (Predictem, Oct 15; Covers Top 25, Oct 17)

Spread: the total opened 41.5 and rose to 43.5, and the low total keeps a 6.5-point favorite in a range where one turnover decides the cover. Per LESSONS, not counted as a separate reason. Neutral. (Predictem, Oct 15)

Spread: analysts split. Covers' Jason Ence's top pick was Kentucky +6.5 (playable to 54%); Covers' Top 25 writer took Oklahoma -5.5 (up to -6.5); Dimers' model projected Oklahoma 26-19 (7). Kentucky has covered 9 of its last 13 (noise per LESSONS). Neutral. (Covers, Oct 16-17; Dimers)
games.reasoning: Oklahoma has the better team and an elite defense, but its offense is among the worst in FBS by success rate. Game-day news then took away its top WR (Livingstone), its top CB (Bowen) and up to three offensive linemen, while Kentucky forces turnovers against a turnover-prone QB. My raw view was Oklahoma by about 3; shaded toward the line it's Oklahoma by 4, so Kentucky +6.5 covers by about 2.5. The decisive angle is the late Oklahoma injury report. Confirmation that Baxter would play would have strengthened this; an early Oklahoma lead with Kentucky's offense stalling on third down is the risk.

research: No. 11 Utah is unbeaten, 5-0 ATS, and has beaten its three Power Four opponents by 21.3 points a game; its offense is 9th in success rate (51.4%). Helps Utah. (Covers Top 25, Oct 17)

Utah QB Devon Dampier completes about 72% with 12 TD and 2 INT; RB Wayshawn Parker averages 7.6 yards per carry with 11 TDs; Utah allows 78.8 rushing yards a game (9th in FBS). Helps Utah. (Predictem)

Colorado is 1-4 ATS, has lost three straight and scores 18.6 points a game (122nd), and only 10.3 against Power Four teams; its offense stays on schedule about 40% of the time. Helps Utah. (Predictem; Covers, Oct 17)

[angle] Colorado starts Isaac Wilson, who spent the past two years at Utah; he knows the Utes' roster and staff, and Colorado had 14 days to prepare off a bye. Helps Colorado. (Covers, Oct 17; Predictem)

[angle] Deion Sanders said Colorado will lean on the run: "We don't want to throw the ball 40-some times"; freshman Kaneal Sweetwyne may also take QB snaps. A slower game helps the underdog. Helps Colorado. (Predictem)
Colorado's defense ranks 3rd nationally in adjusted defensive EPA per play and 2nd in defensive EPA per rush (GameOnPaper). Helps Colorado. (Covers, Oct 17)

[angle] Schedule: PFF ranks Utah's schedule 120th-toughest and Colorado's 9th; Colorado led Texas Tech at halftime and out-gained it before losing 29-7 on a 4-0 turnover margin. Helps Colorado. (Covers, Oct 17)
Utah plays slowly (100th in seconds per play), which means fewer possessions to build a margin; Utah is 2nd in first-quarter points. Mixed. (Covers, Oct 17)
Colorado injuries: WR Danny Scudero (ankle) may not be ready; edge Lamont Lester Jr.'s status unconfirmed. Helps Utah. (Predictem)

Spread: the line has moved from Utah -16.5 to -15.5, -14.5 at the slate, and -13.5 in places, two to three points toward Colorado. Helps Colorado as information, but LESSONS says to treat a big move as fair rather than chase it. (Predictem; Covers, Oct 17)

Spread: SP+ has Utah 7th and Colorado 84th; projections cited Utah 36-14 and 34-16; Predictem took Utah -15.5 and Covers' Top 25 writer took Utah -15.5 (up to -19.5), while Covers' Geoff Clark took Colorado +14.5. Covers' moneyline split was 88% on Utah. Helps Utah. (Predictem; Covers, Oct 17)
Colorado is 8-3 ATS against ranked teams under Sanders (ATS noise per LESSONS; tiebreaker only). Weather: mid-50s, light wind, no rain in Boulder. Neutral. (Covers, Oct 17)
games.reasoning: The models (SP+, two projections around Utah by 20) favor Utah, but the market has moved two to three points toward Colorado, and Colorado has a top-3 defense by adjusted EPA, a bye and a QB who knows Utah's staff. Colorado's offense can't score on good teams, though, which is the bar a 14.5-point underdog has to clear. Shaded to the moved line, I have Utah by about 13.5, within 2 points of the spread, so I pass. Confirmation that Scudero and Lester were both out would have nudged me toward Utah.
games.contaminationNote: Before deciding, a search ("Utah at Colorado preview week 7 2026 Utes injury report...") returned a summary of a Salt Lake Tribune report dated Oct 17, 2026 describing a Utah win at Colorado (RT Kelvin Obot left early with an ankle injury). It gave no score or margin, so I know Utah won but not whether it covered. I had already leaned pass, given the line move toward Colorado against the models, and I kept the pass.

research: No. 21 Wake Forest is second in the ACC after three straight conference wins, 3-0 on the road, and ranked for the first time since 2022 (picked 13th of 17 in the ACC preseason poll). Helps Wake Forest. (Predictem)

Wake QB Gio Lopez has 1,640 passing yards, 16 TD and 1 INT, with nine TDs accounted for in the last two games; WR Carlos Hernandez leads the ACC in receiving yards. Helps Wake Forest. (WagerTalk/GoldSheet, Oct 15; Predictem)

Wake leads the country in offensive net EPA per play; Cal ranks 122nd. Wake is top-20 in both pass success rate (51.2%) and rush success rate (49.5%). Helps Wake Forest. (Covers Top 25 and top picks, Oct 17)
Cal's run defense allows about 175 yards a game (122nd) and ranks 93rd in available yards percentage (51.7%). Helps Wake Forest. (Predictem; Covers top picks, Oct 17)

[angle] Cal's QB is unsettled: Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele (concussion at UNLV) was questionable but expected to clear protocol; coach Tosh Lupoi hadn't named a starter; backup Jackson Brousseau threw for 321 yards with no INT in his first start, vs Virginia Tech. Uncertain; slight help to Wake. (WagerTalk, Oct 15; Predictem; Covers Top 25, Oct 17)

[angle] Cal demoted offensive coordinator Jordan Somerville at halftime against UNLV, and Pat McCann took over play-calling. A program 'that lacks an identity'. Helps Wake Forest. (WagerTalk, Oct 15; Covers top picks, Oct 17)
Cal's defense leads the ACC with 7 interceptions (Kingston Lopa 5, questionable) and has a strong red-zone defense, against a Wake QB with 1 INT. Helps Cal slightly. (Predictem)
Cal RBs Adam Mohammed and Carter Vargas are both questionable. Helps Wake Forest. (Predictem)
[angle] East Coast team on a cross-country trip with a 10:30 PM ET kickoff; Wake has a history of winning out West (at Stanford, Oregon State). Mixed. (Predictem; WagerTalk, Oct 15)

Spread: opened Wake -8.5, peaked at -10 on Oct 12, -9.5 by Oct 15, and -10 on the slate. Early tracked money was 100% on Cal, then 87-89% of spread money on Wake from Oct 14. A 1.5-point move toward the favorite with the money. Helps Wake Forest (priced in). (WagerTalk/GoldSheet, Oct 15)

Spread: SP+ makes Wake about a 13-point favorite; Dimers projected 32-21 (11) with an 80% win chance; Predictem projected 31-20 and would lay up to -11; GoldSheet projected 37-20. Covers' consensus had only 48% on Wake ATS. Helps Wake Forest by 1-3 points vs. -10. (Predictem; Dimers; WagerTalk; Covers)
Cal is 1-3 ATS at home; Wake is 5-1 ATS (noise per LESSONS; tiebreaker only). (Predictem; WagerTalk, Oct 15)
games.reasoning: Wake has the far better offense and Cal's run defense and coordinator turmoil are real problems, but the line has already moved from -8.5 to -10 with the money, and the models land only one to three points past it (SP+ 13, Dimers 11). Shaded toward the line, I had Wake by about 11.5, a 1.5-point edge, with Cal's QB decision unresolved. That's inside my pass band. A confirmed Brousseau start, or an OC change that left Cal's offense in worse shape, would have made it a Wake lean.
games.contaminationNote: I had settled on a pass (Wake by ~11.5, 1.5-point edge) and ran one more search for Cal's QB decision. That search returned an SF Chronicle headline, "Wake Forest clobbers Cal, which opens game with QB Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele on bench", and a summary saying Wake won 41-7 with Brousseau starting. That result was seen BEFORE locking. I kept the pass I had reached before seeing it and did not change it to Wake.
